newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB lifted 3 pct on parent merger rumour.
newsitem.headline: SGB lifted 3 pct on parent merger rumour.

text.p: Shares in Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) jumped almost three percent on Tuesday as speculation mounted that its majority shareholder Cie de Suez is set to merge with Lyonnaise des Eaux.
"I think that those rumours are reflected in the price of the SGB share," said trader Tim Rovencamp at Cera bank's brokerage Nedee & Co.
By 1130 GMT SGB was up 2.85 percent, or 80 francs, at 2,890 francs, with a modest 25 million Belgian francs worth of shares traded.
French newpaper Le Monde reported on Tuesday that water company Lyonnaise des Eaux was set to take over holding group Suez in a planned merger between the two companies.
Suez has a 62 percent stake in SGB.
"People have been buying SGB on speculation, but I see no great benefit for SGB from a merger," said analyst Gert De Mesure at Bank Delen.
"But SGB has a very good dividend yield. This is an element that is positive for investors," he added.
"It's foreign institutional investors that are buying SGB at the moment," De Mesure said.
Dealers added that holding companies in Belgium have lagged recent market rises.
